target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams in sales, customer success, product and engineering who lose focus time to fragmented meetings
problem: Randomly placed meetings and Slack interruptions fragment the workday. Aerotime was a calendar built around weekly goals, time blocking and streamlining team calendars, later described as a shared work tracking feed inside Slack.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat, pricing not found

founders.name: Piyush Narwani
founders.background_notes: Former senior product manager at LinkedIn and a YC alum per TechCrunch. Listed under Former Founders on the YC page.

founders.name: Dhruv Goel
founders.background_notes: Several years at AWS as a senior software development engineer per TechCrunch.

competitors.name: Clockwise
competitors.what: Smart calendar that rearranges meetings to protect focus time
competitors.funding_then: US$18M Series B led by Bain Capital Ventures, June 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Two way calendar sync, scheduling logic and Slack integration are standard engineering with some hard parts in handling many calendar edge cases.

defensibility.rationale: Calendar habits and team data create mild switching costs, but Google Calendar, Outlook and funded smart calendars could ship the same features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in June 2022 noted Google Calendar and Outlook could suggest meeting and focus times; the company is marked Inactive with no acquisition found.

market_need_then: The TechCrunch article and the company frame time fragmentation from meetings and chat as a cost to focused work. No quantified demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Company site is aerotime.com, an exact .com; how it was acquired was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Productivity and flow focus; founder tagline helping humans be in flow every day

branding.community_and_virality: Invite code and access request model on the site; TechCrunch coverage in June 2022. No merch or community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A clean name with an exact .com and one TechCrunch article, but searches for the name return an unrelated aviation news brand, aerotime.aero, which dilutes it.

outcome_analysis: Aerotime joined YC in Winter 2021 with a goal driven calendar and raised a US$2M seed in June 2022 led by Nexus Venture Partners with Sequoia Capital India and SOMA. The YC directory marks it Inactive and the site later described a shared work feed inside Slack, but no shutdown, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The round is stated by TechCrunch (opened) and several outlets in June 2022; one listing dates a seed to April 2021 and CB Insights shows US$2.13M over two rounds, so an earlier small round may be missing. The June 2022 TechCrunch article names Routine, Amie, Rise, Google Calendar and Outlook as alternatives, but it is 16 months after the batch so those are not listed as competitors at founding. Website claims inactive status is not stated; the footer showed 2024. Exit type unknown although YC marks Inactive. Sources disagree on HQ (San Francisco versus Jaipur registry).
